idiom_name: hand-rolled sequence header over POSIX message queues (mq_send / mq_receive)
implementation_notes: Nothing in ISO C provides messaging, let alone grouped delivery, so the three identification fields live in an application-defined header placed in front of each payload (or in a fixed frame layout on a socket) and the receiver keeps a bounded table of per-sequence slots keyed by the sequence identifier. POSIX message queues preserve FIFO order only within one priority level - mq_receive returns the oldest message of the highest priority - so position numbers still carry the ordering. The classic structure is the realization here because there is no runtime or broker client to delegate to.
pitfalls: mq_receive returns the oldest message of the highest priority: never encode position in the priority field, or reassembly breaks as soon as the queue holds parts of different priorities.
Struct layout is platform dependent: serialise each header field explicitly (htonl/ntohl) instead of writing the struct raw to the wire.
Reassembly slots must be bounded and reaped by timeout; an abandoned sequence otherwise pins memory and slots forever.
